newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Volvo unified in period of change.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Volvo unified in period of change.

text.p: The management of Swedish carmaker Volvo is more united then ever in the period of change that the company is going through, Volvo chief executive officer Soren Gyll told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.
"The entire management is working along the same lines. Every division takes its own decisions and they are there after coordinated. Our unity is greater than ever," Gyll said.
Recently Swedish media reports have speculated about a deep division between Gyll and the chairman of the board Bert-Olof Svanholm as well as between different levels within the company.
Volvo is in the process of changing from being a holding company to become a company strictly producing vehicles.

"As assets outside the vehicle production are sold off, Volvo is leaving the role of being a holding company. Traditionally Volvo's division are very independent, but we have to learn to work together more as a group," Gyll said.
Volvo will have to take advantage of possible synergies of the divisions working together and to add their different values together to make a greater sum.

"We have to work across the borders separating the divisions and increase our interaction. The competition in our line of business is very tough and if we can become a little better in many areas, it will bring us a good result," Gyll said.
